before.text:
last section. We want to understand how one can approach the fourth moment via the mean
square of a long Dirichlet polynomial approximation to ζ(s)2. This point of view has also
been explored to a certain extent in the work [H-B] of Heath-Brown, which built upon that
of Ingam and Atkinson [I, A]; see also [CG]. But each of the above used an approximate
functional equation to reduce the necessary length of the approximating polynomial. Here
we want to see what happens purely with Dirichlet polynomials. This perspective will turn
out to be useful in a future discussion of yet higher moments and divisor correlations.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Swap count becomes a phase rule for contour contributions. Pairing the U-swap scale factor with X^s decides whether the contour can be closed to the right with zero contribution or must be moved left across poles, so polynomial length activates residue families in a predictable order.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The six terms are classified as one zero-swap term, four one-swap terms, and one two-swap term. A U-swap term carries a scale factor involving (tT/(2 pi))^{-Us}; together with X^s this compares X with the Uth power of the tT/(2 pi) scale. Below the relevant scale the s-contour is moved right and contributes zero; above it the contour is moved left and the integral is evaluated by residues.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The two-swap family supplies the final residue layer needed for global consistency. Its four shifted poles plus the cutoff pole generate five terms; one cancels the outstanding one-swap artifact, and summing all swap classes removes every dependence on X and restores the fourth-moment recipe.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The two-swap contour integral is zero when the length condition permits moving the contour right. In the longer regime, the displayed Z factor has poles at s=alpha+gamma, alpha+delta, beta+gamma, and beta+delta; together with s=0 these give five residues. The source notes that the last displayed residue is the negative of the last one-swap term. Once the polynomial is sufficiently long, adding zero-, one-, and two-swap contributions cancels all X-dependence and recovers formula (5), consistent with pointwise approximation by the long Dirichlet polynomial.
directed.conceptual_reading: Cutoff-dependent terms are not errors to remove within each swap class; they are interface artifacts designed to cancel across the complete stratification. The two-swap layer is therefore required for closure of the representation, showing why a partial coefficient analysis can look plausible yet omit essential terms.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Contour poles turn the two-swap Euler-product term into a finite residue family. Cross-class cancellation then bridges the X-dependent truncated-polynomial representation to the X-independent shifted fourth-moment formula.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The computation inherits the conditional recipe descent and does not derive the two-swap terms from coefficient correlations. The printed threshold constants and several residue denominators are extraction-sensitive, so the qualitative activation and cancellation are safer than the literal five-term transcription.
directed.uncertainty: The pole set, five-residue structure, cancellation claim, and disappearance of X are explicit. Exact inequalities, constants, and individual factors need scan verification because the source text contains a stray control glyph and formula-level extraction risk.

supported: The span presents a two-swap contour, says that the long regime yields four shifted-factor poles plus the s=0 pole and hence five residues, identifies cancellation with the last one-swap term, and states that summing all swap classes removes X-dependence and recovers formula (5).
The candidate correctly says the calculation inherits the conditional descent and does not derive the two-swap family from coefficient correlations.
inference: Interpreting cutoff-dependent pieces as cross-class cancellation artifacts and the two-swap layer as closure of the full stratification is well supported by the stated cancellation and recovery.
unsupported_or_imported: The candidate repeats the prose's exact positive pole locations, but the displayed factors zeta(1-alpha-gamma-s), and analogues, indicate the opposite sign; the extracted residue display also contains denominator inconsistencies. Exact pole signs are therefore not reliable evidence here.
Calling the pole set itself high-confidence conflicts with the candidate's otherwise appropriate formula-OCR caveat.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: Low: the closure-by-cancellation reading is specific and substantive.
context_or_ocr_risk: A control glyph, inconsistent pole signs, at least one suspect residue denominator, and conflicting threshold typography make literal formula reuse unsafe, though the five-residue structure and cancellation prose remain recoverable.
missed_mechanism: The analysis should distinguish the reliable count and pairing pattern of shifted poles from their extraction-sensitive signed locations.
revision_instructions: Preserve the five-residue, cross-class cancellation, disappearance-of-X, and inherited-conditionality claims, but replace exact signed pole locations with 'four pair-shift poles' and require scan verification before stating their signs or individual residue factors.
